question: What happens when you mutate a property of an object declared with `const user = { name: "Eve" }`?
options: It throws a TypeError because const values cannot change
It succeeds because const locks the memory reference, not the internal properties
It causes undefined to be returned
It only works if you declare the property with var
explanation: const prevents reassignment of the variable binding itself (e.g. user = {}), but does not make the object deeply immutable.
